newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania protests spread in south, minister hurt.
newsitem.headline: Albania protests spread in south, minister hurt.

text.p: Violent protests against failed pyramid investment schemes spread across southern Albania on Saturday as demonstrators torched government buildings and attacked a senior minister.

Albanian state television reported disturbances in eight towns across the region. The worst incidents were in Lushnje, 80 km (55 miles) south of Tirana, where crowds set upon Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu.
Some 5,000 angry protesters surrounded Shehu, chairman of the ruling right-wing Democratic Party, and he was left with blood pouring down his face after a hard object struck him, a witness said.

The minister, a close associate of President Sali Berisha, was trying to calm the situation but apparently misread the mood of the crowd. He fled to the locker room of the town soccer stadium with his bodyguards and plain-clothes policemen.
"Shehu was attacked...when they recognised him. He must have been hit by a stone or hard object because his face is covered with blood," the witness said.
Cameramen came under a hail of stones and protesters set three police trucks on fire. Riot police left the town by helicopter, leaving Shehu behind, witnesses said.
"Down with Berisha!", "We want our money back!" the crowd shouted earlier as it gathered in Lushnje town centre.
In Berat, 40 km (25 miles) south of Lushnje, demonstrators set fire to the town hall, a police station, the prosecutor's office and court buildings, state television said.
"I am sorry for the policemen. They are beating them up. They have also taken the police chief hostage," a woman who lived near the police station said.
Television reported further unrest in the southern towns of Kavaja, Rrogozhine, Gramsh, Tepelena, Memaliaj and Belsh.

The U.S. embassy in Tirana advised U.S. citizens to exercise caution if travelling around Albania and to stay away from crowds as the Interior Ministry ordered the cancellation of soccer matches to stop further potential trouble.
The violence followed two weeks of protests around the impoverished country by angry Albanians who poured their life savings into dubious pyramid investment schemes offering huge returns.
Police used batons to break up the biggest demonstration in the capital Tirana last Sunday but appeared powerless to restore order in the latest outbreak.
About 30 demonstrators were arrested in Lushnje on Friday and police said 29 officers were hurt. There were no immediate figures on any injuries to protesters.

Berisha's Democrats, facing one of their biggest crises since ousting former communists in a general election in 1992, have attempted to appease investors by banning pyramid schemes, setting 20-year prison sentences for their operators and freezing funds. Some fund managers have been arrested.

But such action has infuriated some investors, who argue that some of the money frozen in banks should rightly belong to them. They also say that if scheme operators are jailed, they will never see their cash again.

Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi met with Vehbi Alimucaj, head of VEFA Holding, which operates a high interest investment scheme, to offer it his support, Albanian television said. Meksi said VEFA, which is mainly active in food retail and brewing, had contributed a great deal to the national economy.
